name: CA-26
label: Likely D

key_factors: The district's nine-point Democratic partisan lean provides a structural cushion even with the seat open
Jacqui Irwin holds a decisive fundraising edge over Sam Gallucci, with a large cash-on-hand gap and outside groups aiding her campaign
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold at roughly 96 percent
No public general-election polling exists, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's Democratic lean, Irwin's overwhelming financial advantage, and market pricing near 96 percent all point to Democrats holding this open seat, while Brownley's retirement and the absence of any polling are the main reasons the margin sits below the most bullish readings.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a sharply favorable national environment for the GOP could pull the margin back toward single digits.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
California's 26th District has leaned Democratic by about nine points in recent cycles, and Julia Brownley's retirement leaves an open seat rather than a change in the district's underlying fundamentals. Democrat Jacqui Irwin enters the general election with a substantial financial edge over Republican Sam Gallucci, having raised more than twice as much and holding a far larger cash cushion, with outside groups adding support on her side.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent, and the district's partisan lean gives the party a clear structural buffer. With no public general-election polling available, uncertainty is wider than in a typical safe seat, and the open-seat dynamic adds some risk. Even so, the combination of district lean, fundraising disparity, and market confidence points to Democrats holding the seat in November.
